_note: The six meters that drive every consequence in the game. 0-100 integers. scope 'global' means one value on gameState.meters; 'per-board-member' means one value per roster entry. failsAt null means the meter cannot end the run — board-doubt fails capabilities instead, per design-document §3.

meters.name: Trust
meters.governs: Population belief in leadership's good faith

meters.name: Freedom
meters.governs: Civil liberties; inversely tied to control
meters._note: No failure state of its own. Low freedom angers factions and feeds unrest, which fails through stability.

meters.name: Structural integrity
meters._note: Degrades with excavation and neglect. Crossing collapseRiskThreshold fires level-loss events before the failure state.

meters.name: Morale
meters.governs: Population contentment; feeds stability and productivity
meters._note: NOT in the design document's headline meter table, but referenced constantly in its effect tables ('−morale') and as a population attribute. Declared here as a secondary axis so effects can target it and validation can resolve it. Worth confirming whether this is a first-class meter or a derived read of population state — see the open question in CONVENTIONS.md's companion notes.

meters.name: Legitimacy
meters.governs: Perceived right to rule, distinct from belief in good faith
meters._note: Same status as morale: named in systems-reference §4 (ceremonial fittings, Board chamber, memorials feed it) but absent from the meter table. Distinct from trust — a Chair can be believed sincere and still be seen as having no standing.

meters.name: Board doubt
meters.governs: Advisory Board suspicion, tracked per member
meters._note: Does not fail the run. Above doubtFreezeThreshold a member stops implementing revelations in their domain; above doubtInquiryThreshold they demand the physical text. Chapter 2 only — chapter1.json patches enabled=false.
